summary: Three pages by former members that set out the Divine Light Mission 'light technique' in its two forms. The 1970s form, attributed to the mahatmas' handbook: forefinger on the centre of the forehead, thumb and middle finger pressing each closed eyeball gently, gaze turned toward the centre of the forehead, arms propped on a T-shaped rest (baragon); after some time the initiate should begin to see the 'Divine Light', which the handbook says is seen only through the third eye opened by the Master's grace. The current form, shown by video: the same fingers rest at the inner corners of the lids only to keep the eyeballs still, with an explicit instruction not to press, fifteen minutes per technique, and the word 'light' dropped. A third page lists hatha-yoga texts (shambhavi mudra, yoni mudra) as sources. No results are claimed on these pages.
why_relevant: The clearest available statement of a physical-induction method (eye pressure with upturned gaze) taught as the way to first light, and of its later softening to no pressure; needs the stimulus-independence question asked of it.
